newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - sinks full point overall.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - sinks full point overall.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices sank a full point in Wednesday's sell-off, but have so far managed to avoid heavier losses in the U.S. Treasury market.
Traders said municipals, which were off five to seven basis points at midday, continued following the Treasury market lower throughout the afternoon.
The Treasury long bond was down 1-22/32 at 98-14/32 to yield 6.62 percent, its highest yield since Nov 6.
"They're all getting hit and munis are going down with them," one municipal trader said of the various fixed-income and equity markets.

One muni market analyst, who said overall trading levels were light, said high-grade munis lost only about seven basis points. He said they may have benefited from equity investors fleeing that market. The Dow Jones industrial average ended the day off nearly 71 points, recovering from even steeper losses in the morning.

Among actively traded secondary market munis, bids on Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, Ill., AMBAC 5-1/4s of 2027 were up 10 basis points to 5.72 percent. Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5-1/4s of 2023 were up 10 basis points to 5.68 percent.

Debt futures also ended sharply lower. The March municipal contract lost 1-10/32 to 115-2/32, while March T-bonds were 1-15/32 lower at 112-29/32. The MOB spread widened to 69 ticks from 64 at the close on Tuesday.

Wednesday's repricings included a $219 million Rhode Island Health and Educational Building Corp deal through Bear Stearns & Co. The firm raised yields five basis points in the 2003 and 2004 maturities.
Competitive sales total $368 million in 20 issues. The largest issue is a $78.5 million Virginia housing bond deal at 1100 EST.
Negotiated sales total $809 million in 10 offerings. The largest is a $300 million Alameda County, Calif., deal through MR Beal & Co.

Data releases Thursday include the consumer price index for November at 0830 EST. Economist surveyed by Reuters expect the index to show a 0.3 percent rise overall and a 0.2 percent increaseat the core.
Morgan Stanley & Co restructured $680 million Municipal Assistance Corp for the City of New York bonds, adjusting coupons in the 2002 and 2003 maturities.
In competitive action, Merrill Lynch & Co said it had a $26.5 million balance on New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency's $125 million revenue bond issue.
Thursday's scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales are expected to total $1.2 billion in 30 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
